newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai Refrigerator '96 net up on strong sales.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai Refrigerator '96 net up on strong sales.

text.p: Shanghai Refrigerator Compressor Co Ltd on Thursday reported a 27.17 percent surge in 1996 net profits mainly due to strong sales of air-conditioner compressors.

Analysts said the company is expected to maintain solid growth in 1997 on the back of rapid increases in sales of air-conditioners. But increasing competition may force it to bring down its sales prices.

The company's 1996 net profit was 109.79 million yuan based on international accounting standards, compared with 86.33 million yuan in 1995, according to a company statement in Thursday's Shanghai Securities News.
"The company's profit mainly came from sales of air-conditioner compressors, which accounted for almost 70 percent of its total sales," an analyst with a foreign brokerage in Shanghai said.
The company's sales of air-conditioner compressors surged 86.78 percent to 1.03 million in 1996, giving the firm a 33 percent market share nationwide, the company statement said.
"It will continue to be the main source of profit in 1997, but sales prices will be cut to meet the challenge from more and more new compressor producers," another analyst said.
"According to my estimates, prices will drop five percent in 1997, while sales are expected to increase to compensate for the price reduction," he said.
Analysts said they expect 20 percent growth in demand for quality air-conditioners in eastern China over the next few years.
